newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco do Brasil sees profit in second half.
newsitem.headline: Banco do Brasil sees profit in second half.

text.p: Banco do Brasil President Paulo Cesar Ximenes said the federally controlled bank would show a profit in the second half of this year after posting the country's largest ever commercial loss in the first half.
Banco do Brasil announced a loss of 7.8 billion reais ($7.8 billion) in the first half of 1996, following a loss of 4.2 billion reais ($4.2 billion) in the whole of 1995.

"The first half loss was very large. No matter how hard we work it will be difficult to recover that loss, but the second half figures will show a profit," Ximenes told journalists after a lunch with banking executives in Rio de Janeiro.
"The bank had to make large provisions for loans, but that doesn't mean the loans are lost. The bank's positive result will, in fact, derive partly from the successful recovery of loans."

He said Banco do Brasil was working to gain a greater market share, increase its retail banking business and its share of consumer credit, improve its relations with medium sized and big companies, reduce costs and recover loans.

"As the bank moves more and more into retail banking and increases its share of the consumer credit market and company financing so the proportion of loans to the agricultural sector will fall," Ximenes said. "This does not mean the bank will reduce the actual level of credit it extends to the sector."
The bank currently provides 80 percent of total loans made to Brazil's agricultural sector, and 60 percent of the bank's loans are in that sector, he said.
Ximenes said the shift in the bank's focus away from agribusiness would occur gradually and over time.
He said the bank would work to improve its returns on agricultural loans and to reduce its risks in that sector.

Banco do Brasil has a bad debt problem of $7.2 billion, most of it in the agricultural sector. The Brazilian government in May injected $8 billion into the bank to keep its books within international banking standards.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
